analogs.covers: Almost everything: matrilines led by the eldest cow, male rovers, each family with its own hunting culture, playing with prey

headline: An orca matriline: the eldest mother leads, every family has its own hunting culture, and nothing in the sea is safe.

setting.label: Open sea and coastlines
setting.note: Nomadic. Pods of up to 3 matrilines or sisterhoods migrate and court together, and beach-hunting families patrol the shores.

playsLike: You are an Apex aquatic carnivore. Females live in matrilines of up to 6 related adults led by the mother, or in sisterhoods; males roam in 'rovers' of up to 4 and are more aggressive. You hunt Kaiwhekea, Eurhinosaurus and Leedsichthys before anything else, then Parasaurolophus and Lambeosaurus on the beach or in the water. You may lunge up to a body length out of the water to drag prey in. 2 engage in a hunt or defence. Adult land Apexes are only hunted when they swim, and Spinosaurus and Deinosuchus only in desperate hunger.

why.text: Groups of a mother, her adult children and grandchildren, led by the oldest cow. That is how orca families live (official inspiration).
Each matriline has its own strategy: beaching, chasing or herding prey against underwater cliffs. Orca populations likewise pass down distinct hunting traditions.
Lunges out of the water to clamp prey on the shore, as orcas beach themselves to catch seals.
Noses prey around and blocks it from reaching land before dragging it under. Orcas are notorious for this.
Unpaired males travel in leaderless 'rovers' that are aggressive to other rovers, and solo animals are edgier.

notLike: Orcas answer to no one in the sea; Tylosaurus leaves adult Spinosaurus and Deinosuchus alone unless it is desperately hungry.
twist: Leopard seal (official inspiration) for the lone, edgy ambusher at the shoreline.
